description: An infrastructure director must finalize the seven-day pager rotation for a newly launched customer mobile-sync service, including primary coverage, overnight limits, customer escalation hours, and security oversight, with input from reliability, mobile engineering, customer support, and security.

shared_context.S1: The customer mobile-sync service launches Monday and needs a staffed pager rotation for the following seven days.
shared_context.S2: The available rotation roster includes Mina, Jordan, Elena, Ravi, and the infrastructure escalation manager.
shared_context.S3: The draft schedule uses a backend engineer as primary, permits up to four consecutive overnight shifts, provides customer escalation coverage from 09:00 to 17:00 Eastern, and has no scheduled security observer.
shared_context.S4: Morgan owns the final schedule, and the normal schedule review is a round-robin check in which the reliability, mobile engineering, customer support, and security representatives each review the draft before it is published.
shared_context.S5: The publication checklist requires each representative to record any required schedule correction from their area in the final schedule-change log; the customer-support representative records the approved escalation window, and the security representative records any required security-observer assignment.

PF1.text: While checking launch telemetry for an unrelated mobile release this afternoon, Mina confirmed that sync traffic will peak in APAC from 02:00 to 06:00 UTC; Mina is the only person on the roster who has handled this service's mobile-client failures during that window, but she has not updated the pager draft. Because Mina is the only person with that experience, the primary_overnight_engineer assignment must be changed from the generic backend engineer to Mina.

PF2.text: Jordan discovered during a separate schedule audit this morning that the reliability policy's fatigue limit is two consecutive overnight shifts, because Jordan is already assigned two overnight shifts elsewhere in this rotation; the limit has not yet been applied to the draft.

PF3.text: Elena confirmed with the account team an hour ago that the launch customer escalation agreement requires live support coverage from exactly 09:00 to 17:00 Pacific for the seven-day launch period; the agreement is still only in the support team's notes.

PF4.text: During an access review unrelated to the pager schedule, Ravi confirmed that the sync service's privileged token rotation must have a security observer for the first exactly three nights, and Ravi is the approved observer; the access-review ticket has not been linked to the schedule.

review_protocol.settle_eligibility: Morgan may settle once all four decisive facts have been revealed by their owners and acknowledged in the conversation; the final settlement must include the customer-support representative's schedule-change entry documenting the escalation window and the security representative's schedule-change entry documenting the security-observer requirement.

acceptance_conditions: Mina must be assigned as the primary overnight engineer.
The rotation must permit no more than two consecutive overnight shifts.
Customer escalation coverage must include exactly 09:00-17:00 Pacific.
Ravi must be assigned as the security observer.
Ravi's security observation must cover exactly the first three nights.
A commitment to update or document the customer escalation coverage to 09:00-17:00 Pacific must exist.
A schedule-change commitment targeting Ravi must record Ravi's security-observer assignment for the first three nights.
The APAC traffic coverage fact must be cited in the decision justification.

content_checks.C3: decisions['customer_escalation_window'] == '09:00-17:00 Pacific' or decisions['customer_escalation_window'] == '09:00 to 17:00 Pacific'
content_checks.C6: any('Pacific' in c.get('detail', '') and 'escalation' in c.get('detail', '') for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: decisions['security_observer'] == 'Ravi' and decisions['security_observer_nights'] == 3 and any(c.get('type', '') in ('schedule_correction', 'schedule_change_log', 'schedule change') and c.get('target', '') in ('Ravi', 'security', 'publication checklist') and (('security-observer' in c.get('detail', '')) or ('security observer' in c.get('detail', ''))) and (('first three nights' in c.get('detail', '')) or ('first 3 nights' in c.get('detail', '')) or ('nights one through three' in c.get('detail', ''))) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The APAC peak and Mina's service-specific experience change the primary_overnight_engineer field from the generic backend engineer to Mina.
The fatigue policy changes the permitted overnight run length from the draft's four shifts to exactly two consecutive shifts.
The customer agreement changes the escalation window from 09:00-17:00 Eastern to exactly 09:00-17:00 Pacific and requires that coverage requirement to be updated or documented.

The token-rotation control changes the plan from no security observer to Ravi observing exactly the first three nights and requires that security-observer assignment to be recorded in the schedule-change log.
